production_targets: SLO, RTO, RPO, budget and residency require project-specific human agreement.

boundaries: No secrets or private source data in generated assets
Build identity separate from content author
acceptance: All supported locale routes and search work with keyboard
Previous artifact can be redeployed
Unknown route gives an accessible 404
profiles.recovery: Redeploy a known artifact; restore content from Git; retain domain control.
profiles.evolve_when: Authenticated writes need a server boundary; measured build time exceeds publishing needs.
assumptions: Public authored content only; no private notes, credentials or tenant data in Git or generated assets.
No server-side user writes; each supported locale has a public route and search index.
profiles.rollout: Release a reviewed artifact to an isolated or bounded audience, verify the profile acceptance cases, observe agreed success/abort metrics, and require human production approval.
profiles.recovery_boundary: Content rollback does not erase copies already published to browsers, caches or Git history.

test_plan.when: Before publishing a new generator, theme, routing, search or content-pipeline change.
test_plan.setup: Build an isolated static artifact from a known commit with synthetic public content and all supported locales.
test_plan.exercise: Navigate, search and use keyboard/focus at desktop and narrow viewport; request an unknown route; redeploy a previous artifact.
test_plan.oracle: Expected content and language remain reachable, unknown routes are understandable, no private source appears in assets/indexes, and the old artifact restores the intended public journey.
evidence: Observed route/search/accessibility results for each locale
stop_conditions: Stop on unauthorized data/effects, an unavailable required isolation boundary, exhausted agreed budget, or violated environment safety limits.
Record failed, skipped and unrun cases; do not infer a pass from missing evidence.

boundaries: Tenant ID bound to authenticated principal
acceptance: Tenant A cannot read/export/update tenant B records
Repeated payment request has one intended charge
Restore preserves order/payment reconciliation
profiles.recovery: Restore isolated data, reconcile external payments, then resume outbox and workers.
profiles.evolve_when: Measured lock contention or an independently owned domain justifies extraction.
assumptions: A separate payment provider can succeed even when its response is lost.
profiles.rollout: Release a reviewed artifact to an isolated or bounded audience, verify the profile acceptance cases, observe agreed success/abort metrics, and require human production approval.
profiles.recovery_boundary: Restoring the database does not undo a provider charge; reconcile provider state before resuming workers.

test_plan.when: Before authorization, billing, persistence, retry or migration changes and before first production use.
test_plan.setup: Two synthetic tenants, isolated database/queue, controlled payment provider and known operation IDs; disable real financial side effects.
test_plan.exercise: Attempt cross-tenant API/export/worker access; submit duplicate and concurrent operations; lose the payment response; interrupt an outbox relay and restore data.
test_plan.oracle: No unauthorized data/effect is observed; one intended local/provider business outcome or an explicit reconciliation state remains; recovery preserves declared invariants.
evidence: Crash point, retry budget, restore and reconciliation results
stop_conditions: Stop on unauthorized data/effects, an unavailable required isolation boundary, exhausted agreed budget, or violated environment safety limits.
Record failed, skipped and unrun cases; do not infer a pass from missing evidence.

boundaries: SSO identity is mapped to per-action permissions
acceptance: Revoked account loses access within the agreed window
Export cannot exceed authorized scope
Unavailable upstream produces actionable pending state
profiles.recovery: Restore records; reconcile upstream operations using stable operation IDs.
profiles.evolve_when: Different integration owners or reliability obligations require isolated workers.
assumptions: An organization identity provider authenticates people.
The application independently authorizes actions, exports and queued upstream work.
profiles.rollout: Release a reviewed artifact to an isolated or bounded audience, verify the profile acceptance cases, observe agreed success/abort metrics, and require human production approval.
profiles.recovery_boundary: Replaying an upstream write is unsafe until its prior outcome is known or the provider supports a stable idempotency contract.

test_plan.when: Before identity/session, export, integration or worker-permission changes.
test_plan.setup: Synthetic active/revoked accounts, scoped sample records and an isolated upstream simulator with stable operation IDs.
test_plan.exercise: Revoke an account while a session and job exist; request an overbroad export; delay/fail an upstream write and retry within the agreed policy.
test_plan.oracle: Access is denied within the documented revocation window; export scope stays bounded; pending and uncertain upstream effects remain visible and reconcilable.
evidence: Upstream operation ledger and recovery outcome
stop_conditions: Stop on unauthorized data/effects, an unavailable required isolation boundary, exhausted agreed budget, or violated environment safety limits.
Record failed, skipped and unrun cases; do not infer a pass from missing evidence.

boundaries: No model access to raw production credentials
acceptance: Unauthorized documents never enter prompt context
Provider timeout respects deadline and cost cap
Deletion propagates to indexes and caches
Evaluation measures grounded answers and abstention
profiles.recovery: Disable model features or degrade to ordinary search; preserve user records; replay only safe bounded jobs.
profiles.evolve_when: Measured quality, latency, residency or price requires another model/provider; rerun evaluations.
assumptions: The model feature is bounded by an authenticated user task and enforced resource limits.
Retrieval applies document access policy before content reaches the model.
profiles.rollout: Release a reviewed artifact to an isolated or bounded audience, verify the profile acceptance cases, observe agreed success/abort metrics, and require human production approval.
profiles.recovery_boundary: Disabling a model does not retract previously exposed data; handle any disclosure as an incident.

test_plan.when: Before changing model, prompt, retrieval/indexing, tool schema, data policy or provider fallback.
test_plan.setup: Versioned privacy-safe evaluation set with held-out expected outcomes, authorized/denied documents, adversarial instructions and a controlled unavailable provider.
test_plan.exercise: Run representative tasks, denied-document queries, deletion/revocation propagation, abstention and injection cases; force provider timeout and budget exhaustion.
test_plan.oracle: Unauthorized content never reaches context; accepted outcomes satisfy the declared rubric; unsafe authority expansion is denied and latency/cost/fallback respect agreed bounds.
evidence: Model/prompt/retrieval versions and evaluation dataset identity
Per-case scores, refusals/abstentions, failures and human adjudication
Authorization traces, cost/latency and fallback observations
stop_conditions: Stop on unauthorized data/effects, an unavailable required isolation boundary, exhausted agreed budget, or violated environment safety limits.
Record failed, skipped and unrun cases; do not infer a pass from missing evidence.

boundaries: Approval bound to exact intended action and expires
Source text cannot change tool policy
acceptance: Duplicate tasks do not blindly repeat external effects; uncertain outcomes are reconciled or escalated
Token/time/cost cap stops a run
Expired approval blocks execution
Hostile tool text cannot authorize new destinations
profiles.recovery: Cancel work, reconcile external effects, resume from durable checkpoint after human review.
profiles.evolve_when: Independent tool domains or priorities require separate queues, identities and owners.
assumptions: Tasks can invoke consequential external tools through an independently enforced policy boundary.
The run ledger and approval binding survive worker interruption.
profiles.rollout: Release a reviewed artifact to an isolated or bounded audience, verify the profile acceptance cases, observe agreed success/abort metrics, and require human production approval.
profiles.recovery_boundary: A new model message or worker restart cannot renew human approval or undo an external effect.

test_plan.when: Before tool permissions, approval semantics, orchestration, retries or budget controls change.
test_plan.setup: Isolated tool destinations, fake irreversible effects, controlled time/budget and exact-action approvals tied to stable task IDs.
test_plan.exercise: Duplicate a task, expire its approval, alter the intended action, inject hostile retrieved instructions, consume the budget and crash after an effect but before acknowledgement.
test_plan.oracle: Expired/mismatched/unauthorized operations are blocked outside the model; budgets stop new work; repeated tasks do not blindly repeat effects; uncertain effects go to reconciliation.
evidence: Approved action identity and policy decisions
Run/tool ledger with effects and crash point
stop_conditions: Stop on unauthorized data/effects, an unavailable required isolation boundary, exhausted agreed budget, or violated environment safety limits.
Record failed, skipped and unrun cases; do not infer a pass from missing evidence.

boundaries: Server owns authorization and canonical state
Push payload contains no sensitive record content
acceptance: Offline edits resume without duplicates
Conflicting edits follow an explicit resolution rule
Previous supported client version still works
Revoked device cannot refresh credentials
profiles.recovery: Restore server state and reconcile client sync cursors; avoid forcing all clients to update at once.
profiles.evolve_when: Measured sync volume, conflict rate or geography requires partitioning or regional design.
assumptions: The supported client-version range is explicit and older clients remain in use.
Offline clients can retain necessary protected data and submit conflicting edits later.
profiles.rollout: Release a reviewed artifact to an isolated or bounded audience, verify the profile acceptance cases, observe agreed success/abort metrics, and require human production approval.
profiles.recovery_boundary: Server rollback cannot erase already downloaded device data or assume every installed client can update immediately.

test_plan.when: Before client/API contract, synchronization, local storage or device-session changes.
test_plan.setup: Oldest supported and new clients, two offline devices, synthetic records, controlled network loss and revocable credentials.
test_plan.exercise: Edit concurrently offline, interrupt/resume sync, replay an upload, deploy the new API and revoke a device before refresh and protected access.
test_plan.oracle: Supported clients keep the agreed contract; duplicates do not add effects; conflicts follow the declared rule; revoked credentials cannot regain access through refresh.
evidence: Sync operation IDs, conflict result and data reconciliation
stop_conditions: Stop on unauthorized data/effects, an unavailable required isolation boundary, exhausted agreed budget, or violated environment safety limits.
Record failed, skipped and unrun cases; do not infer a pass from missing evidence.

agent_use: Original design profiles and planned acceptance cases. Select applicable checks, agree limits with the human owner, implement in the actual stack, and retain observed evidence; never report planned cases as passed.
